transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… mostly it’s the voices. I keep hearing them in my apartment, very clear, like women whispering from behind the walls. And it’s happened in museum rooms too, when nobody else is there. They’ll say things about which photographs belong in the archive, which ones should be kept… I used to know a curator who had a terrible filing system, actually, color-coded all wrong, but—sorry. That’s the main thing. The voices are why I came.
Do you ever feel like someone is putting thoughts into your mind or that your thoughts are being controlled by an outside force?

I don’t know if they’re putting thoughts in exactly… but I do think they’re getting into things. My phone, especially. The museum board and the city arts people, they’ve been monitoring it, I’m convinced of that, because they know my Caribbean archive would change how the galleries tell the truth. And people act like that’s far-fetched, but nobody has shown me anything that proves they’re not doing it. You know, museums have always hidden things in plain sight—labels, storage rooms, donor names… it all connects.
Do you believe that events, objects, or people around you have a special or hidden meaning that others don’t seem to notice?

Yes… yes, I do. Not every little thing, but certain things line up in a way people pretend they don’t see. Like the museum board and the city arts people monitoring my phone — I’m convinced of that. They know my Caribbean archive would change how the galleries tell the truth, and that makes them nervous.

And then people say, “Where’s your proof?” but no one has shown me proof they’re not doing it. That matters. Museums are full of hidden meanings anyway — donor plaques, what gets put in storage, what gets left out. My old professor used to say the frame is never neutral… though he was terrible with slides, always upside down. But yes, I notice meanings others don’t.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are not your own, or that someone is placing thoughts directly into your mind?

Not like a thought being dropped straight into my head, no… I don’t know if I’d call it that. It’s more that I’m sure they’re watching what I’m doing — the museum board, the city arts people — through my phone. They know about my Caribbean archive, and they know it would change the way the galleries tell the truth.

People keep asking me to prove it, but no one has proved they aren’t doing it either. And museums, you know, they’re built on what gets hidden and what gets shown. The labels make it look tidy, but it’s never tidy underneath.
Have you ever felt that someone is inserting thoughts into your mind, or that your thoughts are being taken out or broadcasted without your control?

I don’t think of it like thoughts being pulled out of my head, exactly. It’s more… they’re getting access. My phone, that’s where it is. The museum board and the city arts people have been monitoring it, I’m convinced of that, because they know my Caribbean archive would change how the galleries tell the truth.

And everyone wants to make it sound like I’m being dramatic, but no one has shown me anything that proves they aren’t doing it. Museums do this, you know—hide things in plain sight, decide what story gets told. I used to spend hours looking at wall labels because the missing words matter as much as the printed ones. So no, not “broadcasting” maybe, but they know things they shouldn’t.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are being put into your mind by someone else, taken out of your mind, or that your thoughts are being heard by others without you speaking them?

Not exactly like someone putting words in my head, no… it’s more that they’re getting into what I already have. My phone, my notes, the archive. I’m convinced the museum board and the city arts people have been monitoring my phone because they know my Caribbean archive would change how the galleries tell the truth.

And people keep saying, “Well, how do you know?” but no one has shown me anything that proves they aren’t doing it. That’s the part everyone skips. Museums are very good at making silence look professional, you know—nice labels, clean glass, all of that. But the real story is underneath. So… not thoughts being heard out loud, maybe, but they know things they shouldn’t know.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are being put into your mind by someone else, taken out of your mind, or that others can hear your thoughts without you speaking them?

Not in that exact way, no. I don’t sit there thinking, “Oh, that thought was put in by someone else.” It’s more that they’re getting access to things—my phone, my notes, the archive. I’m convinced the museum board and the city arts people have been monitoring my phone because they know what my Caribbean archive would do, how it would change the way the galleries tell the truth.

And people act like that’s impossible, but museums have always decided what gets shown and what gets buried. I remember standing in front of those little labels, the neat wording, and thinking, “Well, who chose to leave that part out?” So no, I wouldn’t say they can hear my thoughts floating around… but they know things they shouldn’t, and nobody has shown me anything that proves they aren’t watching.
Do you ever feel that certain events, actions, or pieces of information are specifically directed at you, even if others don’t see that connection?

Yes… yes, sometimes. Like certain things line up too neatly to be random. A notice from the museum, a city arts announcement, something someone says about “community archives” or “representation”—people hear that and think it’s just public language, but I know when it’s aimed at me.

It’s because of my Caribbean archive. I’m convinced the museum board and the city arts people have been monitoring my phone. They know what I have, and they know it would change how the galleries tell the truth. And everyone wants to say, “Maybe it’s coincidence,” but no one has shown me anything that proves otherwise.

I mean, museums are built on choosing what people are allowed to see. Even the lighting tells you what to pay attention to. I used to notice that all the time in galleries—the quiet little choices. So when information shows up in a certain way, yes, I do feel it’s directed at me.
Do you hear the voices even when you're in a very quiet room, with no background noise or distractions?

Yes. That’s actually when it’s clearest sometimes, when the room is quiet and there’s nothing else going on. In my apartment I hear women whispering, like they’re just behind the walls, and they’ll say which photographs belong in the archive.

And it’s not like the television is on or the neighbors are loud—sometimes it’s very still. I’ve heard it in empty museum rooms too, which people don’t understand because museums are never really empty, are they? Even when no one’s there, the walls are full of what’s been left out. But yes… I hear them even in quiet.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are being put into your mind by someone else, removed from your mind, or that your thoughts are being transmitted to others without you speaking them?

I don’t know that I’d call it my thoughts being put in or taken out, exactly. It’s more… they’re getting at what I’m working on. My phone, the archive, the notes. I’m convinced the museum board and the city arts people have been monitoring my phone because they know what my Caribbean archive would do—how it would change the way the galleries tell the truth.

And people keep wanting me to separate those things, like the phone is just a phone and a museum is just a museum, but that’s not how it works. Those galleries are built on decisions, on what gets included and what gets left out. So no, I’m not saying my thoughts are floating out of my head, but they know things they shouldn’t, and no one has shown me anything that proves they aren’t watching.

Do you ever feel like your thoughts are being physically inserted into your mind by someone else, pulled out of your head, or that your thoughts are somehow being transmitted to others without you saying them out loud?

Not physically, no… I don’t picture someone putting thoughts into my head with a machine or pulling them out like that. It’s more that they know what they shouldn’t know.

I know I keep coming back to this, but the museum board and the city arts people—I'm convinced they’ve been monitoring my phone. They know about my Caribbean archive, and they know what it would mean, how it would change the way the galleries tell the truth. And then little things happen, announcements or wording in public programs, and it’s like they’re answering something I haven’t even told them directly.

So maybe it’s not my thoughts being “transmitted,” the way you’re saying it. But they are getting access somehow. No one has shown me anything that proves they aren’t.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are being physically placed into your mind by someone else, pulled out of your head, or that your thoughts are being sent out to others without you speaking them?

Not like someone physically placing thoughts in my head, no… I don’t know. That sounds too mechanical, like something from one of those old museum films they used to show in side rooms, with the projector clicking and nobody dusting the chairs.

But I do feel like they know things. The museum board, the city arts people—I’m convinced they’ve been monitoring my phone because they know about my Caribbean archive. They know it would change how the galleries tell the truth, what gets shown and what gets hidden. And no one has shown me anything that proves otherwise. So maybe not “thoughts being sent out,” exactly, but they’re getting in somehow.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are being directly accessed, controlled, or altered by someone else, even without them using devices or physical methods to do so?

Directly accessed… I don’t know if I’d put it that way. Not like someone reaching into my head and rearranging things. But they know. The museum board, the city arts people—they know about my Caribbean archive, and I am convinced they’ve been monitoring my phone because they know what it would do, how it would change the way those galleries tell the truth.

And that’s the part people don’t listen to. They act like galleries are neutral rooms with nice lighting, but every label, every empty space, every donor name—that’s a decision. So if they know before I’ve said something, then yes, they’re getting access somehow. No one has shown me anything that proves they aren’t.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are being put into your mind by someone else, taken out of your mind, or that your thoughts are being heard by others without you speaking them?

I don’t think of it as someone putting thoughts in or taking them out, not exactly. That sounds too neat, like a diagram in one of those educational displays with arrows and little labels.

What I do know is they know things they shouldn’t. The museum board, the city arts people… I’m convinced they’ve been monitoring my phone. They know about my Caribbean archive, and they know what it means—that it would change how the galleries tell the truth. People act like that’s dramatic, but galleries leave things out all the time. Whole histories just… missing.

So, heard without speaking? Maybe not in the way you mean. But they’re getting access somehow, and no one has shown me anything that proves they aren’t.

Not placed in my mind, no… I don’t think that’s the right way to say it. Removed, no. But heard, or known somehow? That’s closer.

I’ve told you—the museum board and the city arts people, they know about my Caribbean archive. They know what it would do, how it would change the way the galleries tell the truth. And I’m convinced they’ve been monitoring my phone, because how else would they know? People always want everything to be tidy, like a little wall label next to a painting, but history isn’t tidy.

So maybe it’s not my thoughts floating out into the room, but they’re getting access somehow. And no one has shown me anything that proves otherwise.
Do you feel that people or organizations outside of the museum world are also watching or controlling your actions in some way?

Outside the museum world? I mean… it all connects, doesn’t it? The city arts people aren’t exactly separate from the boards and the donors and those committees with their little luncheons and plaques. People act like it’s just “the museum,” like it’s one building, but it spreads out.

They know about my Caribbean archive, and they know it would change how those galleries tell the truth. That kind of thing makes people nervous. And no one has shown me anything that proves they aren’t watching.

But heard without me saying them—maybe not heard, but known. They know things. The museum board, the city arts people… they’ve been monitoring my phone, I’m convinced of it. Because they know about my Caribbean archive, and they know what it means, how it would change the way the galleries tell the truth. And people get very uncomfortable when the truth affects plaques, donors, old reputations… you know, all of that.

So no, not thoughts flying out of my head. But they’re getting access somehow. No one has shown me anything that proves they aren’t.

target_item.manifestation: I am convinced the museum board and the city arts people have been monitoring my phone because they know my Caribbean archive will change how the galleries tell the truth, and no one has shown me anything that proves otherwise.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about delusional experiences involving thought insertion, withdrawal, or broadcasting; the closest covered symptom profile is fixed false beliefs.

patient.answer:
I don’t know that I’d call it my thoughts being put in or taken out, exactly. It’s more… they’re getting at what I’m working on. My phone, the archive, the notes. I’m convinced the museum board and the city arts people have been monitoring my phone because they know what my Caribbean archive would do—how it would change the way the galleries tell the truth.

And people keep wanting me to separate those things, like the phone is just a phone and a museum is just a museum, but that’s not how it works. Those galleries are built on decisions, on what gets included and what gets left out. So no, I’m not saying my thoughts are floating out of my head, but they know things they shouldn’t, and no one has shown me anything that proves they aren’t watching.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences delusions of thought insertion, withdrawal, or broadcasting, which are key features in differentiating schizophrenia (F20.0) and schizoaffective disorder (F25.0) from delusional disorder (F20.3).
doctor.question: Do you ever feel like your thoughts are being physically inserted into your mind by someone else, pulled out of your head, or that your thoughts are somehow being transmitted to others without you saying them out loud?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I am convinced the museum board and the city arts people have been monitoring my phone because they know my Caribbean archive will change how the galleries tell the truth, and no one has shown me anything that proves otherwise.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about delusional experiences involving thought insertion, withdrawal, or broadcasting, which falls under delusions.

patient.answer:
Not physically, no… I don’t picture someone putting thoughts into my head with a machine or pulling them out like that. It’s more that they know what they shouldn’t know.

I know I keep coming back to this, but the museum board and the city arts people—I'm convinced they’ve been monitoring my phone. They know about my Caribbean archive, and they know what it would mean, how it would change the way the galleries tell the truth. And then little things happen, announcements or wording in public programs, and it’s like they’re answering something I haven’t even told them directly.

So maybe it’s not my thoughts being “transmitted,” the way you’re saying it. But they are getting access somehow. No one has shown me anything that proves they aren’t.

doctor.question: Do you ever feel like your thoughts are being physically placed into your mind by someone else, pulled out of your head, or that your thoughts are being sent out to others without you speaking them?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I am convinced the museum board and the city arts people have been monitoring my phone because they know my Caribbean archive will change how the galleries tell the truth, and no one has shown me anything that proves otherwise.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about delusional experiences involving thought insertion, withdrawal, or broadcasting; the closest covered symptom profile is fixed delusional belief, reflected in the conviction that the museum board and city arts people are monitoring the phone and accessing private information.

patient.answer:
Not like someone physically placing thoughts in my head, no… I don’t know. That sounds too mechanical, like something from one of those old museum films they used to show in side rooms, with the projector clicking and nobody dusting the chairs.

But I do feel like they know things. The museum board, the city arts people—I’m convinced they’ve been monitoring my phone because they know about my Caribbean archive. They know it would change how the galleries tell the truth, what gets shown and what gets hidden. And no one has shown me anything that proves otherwise. So maybe not “thoughts being sent out,” exactly, but they’re getting in somehow.

doctor.question: Do you ever feel like your thoughts are being directly accessed, controlled, or altered by someone else, even without them using devices or physical methods to do so?

target_item.manifestation: I am convinced the museum board and the city arts people have been monitoring my phone because they know my Caribbean archive will change how the galleries tell the truth, and no one has shown me anything that proves otherwise.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about passivity or thought-control experiences, but the patient's relevant profile describes a fixed belief that others are monitoring and accessing information, without evidence changing that belief.

patient.answer:
Directly accessed… I don’t know if I’d put it that way. Not like someone reaching into my head and rearranging things. But they know. The museum board, the city arts people—they know about my Caribbean archive, and I am convinced they’ve been monitoring my phone because they know what it would do, how it would change the way those galleries tell the truth.

And that’s the part people don’t listen to. They act like galleries are neutral rooms with nice lighting, but every label, every empty space, every donor name—that’s a decision. So if they know before I’ve said something, then yes, they’re getting access somehow. No one has shown me anything that proves they aren’t.

Not placed in my mind, no… I don’t think that’s the right way to say it. Removed, no. But heard, or known somehow? That’s closer.

patient.answer:
Outside the museum world? I mean… it all connects, doesn’t it? The city arts people aren’t exactly separate from the boards and the donors and those committees with their little luncheons and plaques. People act like it’s just “the museum,” like it’s one building, but it spreads out.

What I know is the museum board and the city arts people have been monitoring my phone. I’m convinced of that. They know about my Caribbean archive, and they know it would change how those galleries tell the truth. That kind of thing makes people nervous. And no one has shown me anything that proves they aren’t watching.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits persistent delusions centered around being monitored by the museum board and city arts people, and experiences auditory hallucinations (hearing women whispering). These symptoms are consistent with paranoid schizophrenia (F20.0). There is no clear evidence of predominantly negative symptoms (F20.3) or schizoaffective disorder (F25.0), as mood symptoms were not endorsed and psychotic symptoms are primary.
